## Solution

Let $M = 10^k - 1$ and $t = M/\gcd(N,M)$. Then $t$ divides $M$, so $\gcd(t,10)=1$. Writing $N = n\cdot\frac{M}{t}$ with $\gcd(n,t)=1$ gives $\frac{N}{M} = \frac{n}{t}$.

**Reduction to decimal expansions.** Since $N < 10^k$, the $k$-digit block of $N$ (with leading zeros) is the first $k$ digits after the decimal point of $n/t$. Because $11235$ contains no zeros, it appears in $N$ exactly when it appears in those first $k$ digits. So $N$ contains $11235$ if and only if some digit window of $n/t$ reads $11235$.

A window starting after $j$ digits reads $11235$ exactly when
$$\{10^j n/t\} \in [0.11235,\ 0.11236).$$
The fractional part equals $a/t$ with $a \equiv 10^j n \pmod t$, so some fraction $a/t$ lies in $[0.11235, 0.11236)$. Its reduced denominator is at most $t$. Hence $t$ is at least the smallest denominator of any fraction in that interval.

**Lower bound.** The fraction $10/89 = 0.\overline{11235955056179775280898876404494382022471910}$ lies in the interval. Its distance from the interval's endpoints is at most $\approx 9.6\times 10^{-6}$ on the left and $\approx 4.5\times 10^{-7}$ on the right. Any fraction $p/q \neq 10/89$ satisfies
$$\left|\frac pq - \frac{10}{89}\right| \ge \frac{1}{89q}.$$
For $q \le 88$ this is at least $\frac{1}{89\cdot 88} \approx 1.28\times 10^{-4}$, which exceeds $9.6\times10^{-6}$. So no fraction with denominator $\le 88$ lies in the interval. Therefore $t \ge 89$.

**Achieving 89.** The number $1/89$ has period $44$, so $89 \mid 10^{44}-1$. Let $Q = (10^{44}-1)/89$ and take $N = 10Q$. Then:
- $N = \dfrac{10}{89}(10^{44}-1)$ begins with $11235\ldots$, since $10/89 = 0.11235955\ldots$, so $N$ contains $11235$.
- $N < 10^{44}$, so $k=44$ is valid.
- $\gcd(N, 10^{44}-1) = \gcd(10Q, 89Q) = Q\cdot\gcd(10,89) = Q$.
- Therefore $\dfrac{10^{44}-1}{\gcd(N,10^{44}-1)} = \dfrac{89Q}{Q} = 89$.

The minimum is $89$.

ANSWER: 89
